description:
Advances: ancora.gate

Severity: Medium (calibrated). Consolidated findings F14, F49, F53, F54, F55, F56, F57, F58, F65. Cannot have landed on the shipped branch: these are test-quality changes on code that already merged, and several need new fixtures.

The theme: several tests pass for reasons orthogonal to what they claim, and the two guards that enforce ancora architectural charter are vacuous if their matchers ever break.

F14 (the important one) — both static charter guards are of the form assert offenders == [] with NO positive control, so they would stay green forever if their AST matchers stopped matching. forbidden_spawner_test also resolves its root at runtime, so a file glob that matches nothing passes silently. Fix: pin the root at compile time with a module attribute, add a non-empty floor to both guards so an empty candidate set fails, and give each detector a positive control asserting it fires on a known offender before the allowlist excludes it.
F65 — related and worth doing in the same pass: the no-execution guarantee rests on all eight mix tasks declaring the deps.loadpaths requirement, which keeps the target build off the code path, and NOTHING tests that. Changing one task to compile would weaken the charter with no failing test. Add a static test asserting every mix task declares exactly that requirement, in the style of the existing guards.
F49 — scope the exactly-eight-tasks comparison to Application.spec(:ancora, :modules) so the no-task-under-any-other-name clause is actually asserted.
F54 — replace the is_function/2 tautology with Code.ensure_loaded!/1 plus function_exported?/3, matching the three siblings in the same directory. As written it passes with the function deleted.
F55 — anchor the review grouping assertions with the String.split technique the same file already uses at line 112, or rename the test to what it actually covers: today it asserts on a hand-built view model rather than the grouping code.
F56 — give spec_next_test a fixture project and --root, and assert a specific classification rather than whatever the working tree happens to hold.
F57 — add test/ancora_test.exs covering Ancora.validate/2 directly: one warning-level finding, fail false without strict and fail true with it, plus the checked counts. It has an external caller and no direct test.
F53 — assert growth and shrink suppression under acknowledgment, and the never-raise guard, under the ancora.gate.acknowledgment_clears tag.
F58 — delete the six dead moduletag tmp_dir lines.

Deliberately dropped by the review, do not relitigate: a style sweep over assertion failure messages that do not name what broke, with no defect behind it.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/static/forbidden_spawner_test.exs and forbidden_writer_test.exs (positive controls, compile-time root, non-empty floor), a new static test asserting every mix task declares the deps.loadpaths requirement (tagged to the no-execution requirement in ancora.gate or ancora.tasks), test/ancora/static/exactly_eight_test.exs scoped to Application.spec(:ancora, :modules), the is_function/2 tautology replaced, test/ancora/review_test.exs grouping assertions anchored, test/mix/tasks/spec_next_test.exs on a fixture with --root, a new test/ancora_test.exs for Ancora.validate/2, growth/shrink suppression and never-raise under ancora.gate.acknowledgment_clears, six dead moduletag tmp_dir lines deleted
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) each charter guard fails when its allowlist is emptied against a known offender and fails when the candidate set is empty (prove both in the IMPLEMENTED comment by temporarily breaking the matcher and showing the red run); (2) changing one mix task's requirement away from deps.loadpaths makes a test fail; (3) the exactly-eight test asserts no task exists under any other name; (4) the review grouping test exercises the grouping code, not a hand-built view model; (5) spec_next asserts a specific classification on a fixture; (6) Ancora.validate/2 has direct coverage of strict and non-strict verdicts and counts
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: each charter guard fails on a known offender and on an empty candidate set, and every mix task provably declares deps.loadpaths.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- test/** (this is a test-only ticket)
- .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md (tag, scenario, and verification-block edits only)

- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base <your base>` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator after the fifth admission defect of this epic. Derivation is file-scoped: every production function called anywhere in a test file joins every subject tagged anywhere in that file, and siblings merging into the epic tip change that set under you, so no list written at admission stays correct. Rule: acknowledgment edits only. Write one substantive requirement or scenario statement describing what THIS ticket changed as THAT subject observes it, verified by execution that the named input actually reaches that subject. Never restate another subject's contract in a second home, never weaken a must, never delete a requirement, never use a Spec-Ack trailer for it. If the subject genuinely observes no change from your work, say so in your completion record and stop; that is an escalation to the orchestrator, not a failure. Every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; an affects: entry on your own ADR is the expected form.)
- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

- .spec/decisions/** (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator, third instance of the same admission defect, this one found by the ancora-xla.4 verifier. Ancora.PolicyFiles.missing_decision?/1 at lib/ancora/policy_files.ex:115 fires change/missing_decision whenever any path under .spec/specs/ changes without an accompanying decision-record change in the SAME diff. Every ticket here is required to edit a spec, so this finding is structurally guaranteed and the decision-record edit is forced rather than optional. Write a real contract statement describing what you actually built; do NOT add a hollow line to silence the finding, which a grader will read as finding-silencing and bounce.)

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/** (read-only; if a new test exposes a real production defect, comment it on this ticket and file a child under ancora-xla instead of fixing it here)
- priv/**
- docs/**

Out of Scope (intent):
- no assertion-message style sweep (dropped by the review)
- no merging of the two git fixture helpers (dropped by the review)
- assertional test edits here are the point; expect the critical grader path

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket


SCOPE ADDITION (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 21:05), from the ancora-xla.2 Elixir test critic. This ticket's subject is giving thin tests real teeth, and these are four conditional clauses with no test at all, on surfaces ancora-xla.2 created or touched.

1. lib/ancora/derive.ex:125. The `catch kind, reason -> {:error, {:resolver_throw, ...}}` sibling of the rescue clause that IS tested. A closure that throws rather than raises closes it.
2. lib/ancora/gate.ex:423 and the :cat_file_batch_timeout arm of run_context_error/1 at :408. Both untested. This matters beyond coverage arithmetic: ancora-xla.2's behaviour item (4) claims it "maps EVERY RunContext.start/3 failure to {:env, message}", and that claim is currently proved for one atom out of three.
3. lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex:71, the `rescue ArgumentError -> close(port); {:error, :port_poisoned}` path. The new poisoning test does not reach it, because it returns earlier at the Port.info == nil guard on :50.
4. lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex:31, open/1 returning :git_executable_not_found. Untested; the existing PATH-rewrite test covers Git.run/2 only.

Two smaller items from the same review, both in test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs and both about the unreadable-input test ancora-xla.2 added:
- :80 asserts `result.stdout =~ relative`, which pins that the diagnostic names the file but not why it failed. Adding the permission-denied text or the remedy string would stop an unrelated future environment failure that happens to mention the path from satisfying this assertion.
- :74-87 runs two subprocess cases inside one `for`, so the lib/ case never runs if the test/ case fails and one bug hides the other. Two named tests give independent signal.

Also noted and NOT assigned anywhere, because it is genuinely fine: close/1's bounded wait at batch_port.ex:100-116 has no direct test, but ancora-xla.2 correctly reverted the vacuous 10 millisecond exit-status receive back to a port monitor with a 500 millisecond bound, and three independent measurements confirmed the revert. Coverage there would be nice rather than necessary.

Add whichever of the above your Allowed touches already cover; the four conditional clauses are the ones that matter, since they close a claim this epic has already shipped once as overstated.
title: Give the static guards and thin tests real teeth
